Rain doesn’t have to stop a remodel, but it does change how a project is planned. Here is how LRL Builders approaches work on Walnut Creek homes during the wet season. Scheduling comes first. Exterior work like roofing, siding, windows, and framing is sequenced around the forecast, so openings in the home aren’t left exposed when rain is coming. Protection on site matters just as much. Tarps and temporary coverings keep water out of open walls and roof areas, and materials like lumber, drywall, and flooring are stored off the ground and kept dry. Wet materials can swell, warp, or grow mold, so they are not installed until they are ready. The inside of your home gets attention too. Floor protection and clean entry paths keep mud and moisture from being tracked through the house. Drainage is another focus. Water directed away from the foundation, work areas, and new construction helps prevent problems both during the project and long after. Finally, communication. If weather shifts the schedule, you hear about it early, with an updated plan. See how LRL Builders plans remodeling projects in Walnut Creek.
